gaps.sentence: Don't worry, I ___ you with the boxes as soon as I arrive.
gaps.hint: a promise made about the future
gaps.explanation: A promise about the future uses 'will' in the main clause: will help.

gaps.sentence: This time next week I ___ on a beach in Portugal, with my phone switched off.
gaps.hint: this time next week means in progress
gaps.explanation: 'This time next week' points to an action in progress at a future moment, so the future continuous fits: will be lying.

gaps.sentence: There ___ a cinema on this corner, but it closed years ago.
gaps.hint: a past state that has ended
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' is also used for past states that no longer exist: used to be.

gaps.sentence: He rarely ___ his laptop on Sundays because he prefers to rest.
gaps.explanation: Frequency adverbs such as 'rarely' mark habitual actions, which take the present simple: uses.

gaps.sentence: Who ___ this bag belong to? It has been sitting here all morning.
gaps.hint: the question form needs auxiliary does
gaps.explanation: Present simple questions need the auxiliary 'does' plus the base verb: does this bag belong to.

gaps.sentence: The soup ___ delicious, but I think it needs a little more salt.
gaps.hint: taste describing a quality is stative
gaps.explanation: When 'taste' describes a quality of something, it is a state verb: tastes.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her laptop repaired twice this year already.
gaps.explanation: 'Has had it repaired twice this year' — present perfect of causative have.

gaps.sentence: Look at the time! We ___ discussing one agenda item for an hour.
gaps.explanation: 'For an hour' and still relevant — present perfect continuous.
